derived: GSK turned 18.02% of revenue into free cash over 2023 to 2025 against the 19.3% its filed expense lines leave. Checked before interest: interest paid is booked under financing, so free cash flow is already struck before interest, so the charge stands. Restated at replacement capex: GSK spent 4,061mm GBP on plant over 2023 to 2025 against 2,628mm GBP of plant depreciation, 1.52% of revenue above what keeps the plant running. Taken at depreciation, the charge falls from 1.44% to 0.00%. Restated without one-off cash: GSK's free cash flow over 2023 to 2025 carried 1,867mm GBP of legal settlements. None recurs, so the charge stays nil. Restated to the amortisation floor: the filed cost lines leave a 21.54% pre-tax margin where the cash over 2023 to 2025 supports 23.77%, so the charge rebuilds at -2.23%. It was held at nil, but GSK books 808mm GBP of non-cash amortisation of acquired intangibles inside its cost lines in FY2025 (0001131399-26-000004), 2.47% of revenue, so the charge takes the rebuilt figure: -2.23%. Restated without working capital build: over 2023 to 2025 GSK's cash flow statement shows receivables up 1,109mm GBP, inventories up 858mm GBP, payables down 63mm GBP, a working capital build of 2,030mm GBP, 2.15% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge falls from -2.23% to -2.47%.

the programme is finished and did not produce a result. ZEST (NCT04915755), a Phase 3 of niraparib against placebo in participants with HER2-negative BRCA-mutated or triple-negative breast cancer and detectable circulating tumour DNA after definitive therapy, was closed without reaching its randomisation target: of more than 2,700 stage I-III patients prescreened, about 8% were ctDNA positive and nearly half of those already had radiographically detectable disease, so only 40 participants were randomised (reported at the San Antonio Breast Cancer Symposium, December 2024; American Association for Cancer Research news release, 'ZEST Trial Offers Insights for Using ctDNA to Predict Breast Cancer Recurrence', aacr.org). The registry still reads 'Active, not recruiting' with 40 enrolled, a primary completion of 2024-06-28 and a last update of 2025-07-16 (ClinicalTrials.gov API v2, read 2026-10-27), which is why the book carried it as a live Phase 3. The only other breast study GSK runs on niraparib is NCT04641247, a long-term treatment extension for participants who completed a prior GlaxoSmithKline or TESARO niraparib study, which opens no new indication
